category: error tracking and application monitoring (hosted), sponsored plan for students and teachers

free_tier.stated: Education sponsorship, free for 1 year, for students who hold a GitHub Student Developer Pack and for teachers who use Sentry in class: 50K errors, 5GB logs, 5GB application metrics, 5M spans, 500 replays, 1 cron monitor, 1 uptime monitor, 750 continuous profile hours, 1 UI profile hour, 1GB of attachments, 100 size analysis uploads per month and 1 Seer active contributor seat, with unlimited projects and members
free_tier.notes: Counted per event category: errors, spans and replays are event counts, logs, application metrics and attachments are GB, and each quota is stated per month. The Sentry for Education page lists 50K errors, 5GB logs, 5M spans, 500 replays, 1 cron monitor, 1GB attachments and USD 20 of Seer credits a month. The Sentry for Good page lists 1 Seer active contributor seat instead. A Pay-As-You-Go budget for volume past the quotas needs a credit card on the account.

per_object_cap.stated: Spans are limited to 20KB, a Team plan change that a help article applies to the education sponsored plan
per_object_cap.notes: The size-limits guide of the Sentry docs names no plan. It rejects events over 200KB compressed or 1MB decompressed and minidump uploads over 40MB compressed or 200MB decompressed, all files combined.

retention.stated: 30 days for spans, logs and profiles: a help article applies the changes listed for Team plans to the education sponsored plan, and that list includes 30 day retention of spans, logs and profiles. The retention of errors and the other data types on the education plan is unverified: the retention table has no education column, and its Team column gives errors 90 days.
retention.notes: The retention table of the Sentry docs has columns for the Developer, Team, Business and Enterprise plans and none for a sponsored plan.

egress.terms: not stated: the plan pages list ingested volumes and name no charge for reading data back

interface_detail: The Sentry web API gives programmatic access to the platform and the SDKs have a separate API surface; whether the education plan includes web API access is not stated on the plan pages
tooling: the Sentry SDKs and the Sentry web API
chaining: An error and tracing sink for jobs on free compute, with 50K errors and 5M spans a month for 1 year, reachable only with a GitHub Student Developer Pack or a teacher application; without one, the free Developer plan (dev-services/sentry) is the hosted fallback.

limits.value: Activation needs a linked GitHub account that holds the Student Developer Pack, which the GitHub Education team grants after it reviews proof of current student status; a teacher applies and Sentry support names the documents required
50K errors, 5M spans and 500 replays per month on the education plan
5GB of logs, 5GB of application metrics and 1GB of attachments per month on the education plan
Spans are limited to 20KB on the education plan, a Team plan change that a help article applies to it
30 days of retention for spans, logs and profiles on the education plan

limits_note: 1 cron monitor, 1 uptime monitor, 750 continuous profile hours, 1 UI profile hour, 100 size analysis uploads per month and 1 Seer active contributor seat. The Team plan changes that a help article applies to the education plan add 20 custom dashboards and a maximum of 20 metric monitors. The plan lasts 1 year from its start date and is not renewed: the organization then moves to the free Developer plan. One user activates one education plan, and a sponsorship covers one organization.
binding_note: The plan activates only for a GitHub account that holds the Student Developer Pack, which GitHub grants on proof of current student status, so the monthly quotas bind only after that gate.

identity_cost.detail: Students need a Sentry account with at least one organization, a linked GitHub account and an active GitHub Student Developer Pack. The Sentry sign-up form asks for name, organization, email and password behind a reCAPTCHA and has no card field. The activation page asks a user to sign in, associate GitHub and activate, and names no card step. GitHub grants the pack to a user enrolled in a degree or diploma program, such as a high school, college, university or homeschool, who shows a school ID with an enrollment date, a class schedule, a transcript or an enrollment verification letter, and who verifies an academic email address where the school requires one. Teachers apply for a sponsored account. Sentry support reviews the application and names the documents required, for example a screenshot of a GitHub Education account that shows active Faculty or Teacher benefits. GitHub states that teachers are not eligible for the pack, and its teacher application asks for a school-issued email address and documents that prove school affiliation. One user can activate one education plan.

reliability_note: events past the quota are not accepted until the next usage period unless a Pay-As-You-Go budget is added; the plan ends after 1 year and the organization moves to the free Developer plan
confidence_note: The quotas, the term and the eligibility steps come from first-party Sentry pages and help articles. The span size limit and the 30 day retention of spans, logs and profiles follow from two sentences of one help article, which applies the Team plan changes to the education plan. The retention of errors, the plan name shown in the app and web API access need an activated organization and are unverified.

notes: Two routes lead to the same quotas. A student activates the plan at sentry.io/for/education/ with a GitHub Student Developer Pack. A teacher applies for a sponsored account that Sentry support reviews. A help article applies the changes listed for Team plans to the education plan, so the plan carries Team features. The free Developer plan is dev-services/sentry. The open source and non-profit sponsorship plan is compute/sentry. The pack listing at education.github.com/pack words the offer as 50K errors, 100K transactions, 1GB attachments, 500 replays, Team features, a 1 year limit that can renew and on-demand disabled. The Sentry help articles say the plan is not renewed and that a credit card enables Pay-As-You-Go.
